observedFacts.finding: diagnostic.echo reads message/injectError/errorMessage and returns without a delay/hold branch. The response copies the request generation. Extra delay-like parameters are unused, not an implemented capability.
The real RN root awaits the actual facade, then calls the actual native module deliverResponse. It exposes no response-hold/release controller.

Normal production send uses onSefariaRPCRequest; deliverResponse queues the actual bridge response handler. setJSExecutor/customExecutor is a replacement route and is not acceptable as evidence of the original Hermes path. DEBUG response logging does not itself acknowledge the actor's actual late-ignore decision.

Explicit stale calls reject before dispatch. All observed session-epoch/transport transitions cancelAll and remove pending continuations before publication. A subsequently delivered old response therefore normally hits the missing-request return at402-405; the separate response-generation mismatch at428-435 applies while its request still exists.

The original reset performs resetState then original bumpSessionEpoch within the retained lifecycle boundary. A late-reply test must observe that real operation, not mutate private generation storage or force a pending request to survive cancellation.

surface.awaitVisible legitimately waits for the exact first original mount/readiness/layout under a bounded deadline. It is not a diagnostic delay parameter. Inventing a never-owned surfaceID merely to make it wait is not acceptance of an original UI lifecycle.

Strict-response and concurrent-delay controls use MockBridgeTransport/ConcurrentEchoTransport. They are component boundaries, not live Hermes acceptance. This audit did not rerun or certify those historical tests.
